Create your coin

1. Front photo   →   2. Back photo   →   3. Crop and turn upright   →   4. Preview and save

Photograph each coin from straight above, front first, then back. A plain surface or your open palm both work.

Soft light makes the best coins. Stand near a window, out of direct sun, and turn off the lamp overhead. Bright reflections on enamel photograph as white streaks; if one slips through, paint it out with the glare brush on the next screen. If you need the flash, tilt the phone a little instead of shooting straight down: the flash bounce misses the lens, and the tool straightens the coin afterwards.

Next photo: front

What shape is this coin?
Stationary preview: check lettering is upright

Drag each circle onto the coin and set its size. Then turn each side until the TOP marker sits at the top of the coin.

Crop missed the coin? Draw a box around it and the crop snaps to the coin inside.

A white streak of reflected light on the enamel? Paint over it on either photo and it is filled in from the colours around it.

Paint over the white reflection on the photo below. The fix appears as you paint, and the outline shows what you have covered. Keep strokes tight: the fill borrows nearby colours, so painting across lettering or stars smudges them.

A clear lacquer layer that catches the studio lights. Raise it for domed or enamel coins, lower it for bare antique metal.
Higher keeps enamel colors and lettering readable at every angle. Lower looks more like bare metal.
Drag to turn and tilt. Scroll or pinch to zoom; double-click to reset.

The GLB is a portable 3D coin with both photos embedded; open it in a compatible 3D viewer to rotate it. Both GIFs are just the coin, with a see-through background. Email signature offers a 120 px GIF, a still PNG, and Outlook setup steps. Coin GIF is 360 px for posts and profiles. Video is 1080 px square on the wall background, since video can't be see-through.
